summary: Both sides render a single flat, uniform, perfectly static warm-orange across every rig/seed/fps/time window tested; the port's constant is paler and slightly yellower than the original's (RGB 255,146,39 vs 255,106,12 — hue +6.5 deg, saturation -0.11, mean brightness +18%).
observations: Structure: both sides paint EVERY pixel the same single colour. A --dump of all 60 strip pixels at t=0/3/5.9 s gives exactly 1 unique RGB value per side per frame on both sides — no gradient, no spatial variation, no per-pixel noise.
Original constant: RGB (255,106,12) — deep amber. HSV approx (23.2 deg, S 0.953, V 1.0). meanBrightness 124, meanR 255 / meanG 106 / meanB 12.

Port constant: RGB (255,146,39) — lighter orange. HSV approx (29.7 deg, S 0.847, V 1.0). meanBrightness 147, meanR 255 / meanG 146 / meanB 39. So the port is +40 on green and +27 on blue, i.e. ~16% and ~11% of full scale respectively.

Motion: identically dead on both sides. motion avg/min/max = 0 and motionLit avg/min/max = 0, with zeroMotionFrames = 100% of captured frames, on EVERY run: baseline (6 s / 20 fps, 120 frames), survey (60 s / 5 fps, 300 frames), survey-240 (240 s / 2 fps, 480 frames), fps10, fps40. brightnessTrend 'steady' on both. This is genuine stasis, not the dim/sparse false-freeze: meanBrightness is 124/147, far above the noise floor, and consecutive-frame dumps are byte-identical.
No warm-up transient and no late-window decay: steady-late (--skip 20 --seconds 30 --fps 4) gives the same two constants, first == last == avg on every series for both sides.

Time-of-day sweep: I stepped a warm-up of 0 / 3600 / 10800 / 21600 / 32400 / 43200 / 54000 / 64800 / 75600 / 86400 simulated seconds (--skip at --fps 1) and dumped the frame at each. BOTH sides returned their same constant at all ten points, including a full 24 h span. The harness pins wallClock at 1756000000 and that pinned clock does not advance with simulated elapsed time, so a clock-driven colour-temperature curve — which the pattern name implies — cannot be exercised from output. Both sides agree at the one clock instant the harness can show, and neither drifts with elapsed run time.

Sensors: meta.json reports wantsSensors=false on BOTH sides, so the engines say neither pattern binds any sensor global (light, accelerometer, frequencyData). Forcing --sensors synth (beat120) anyway changed nothing: dumps at t=0 / 4.15 / 9.25 s are the same two constants on both sides. Agreement, not divergence.

Lens independence: the constants are identical under --seed 7, --seed 1234, --seed 99999 (all 1 unique colour per side, same values as seed 1); under --rig grid --grid 16x16 (256 px, 1 unique colour per side); and under --pixels 600 (1 unique colour per side). Neither side has any pixel-count, rig-shape, or RNG dependence.
fps: irrelevant here — both sides are constant at 5, 10, 20 and 40 fps, so there is no frame-rate-coupling question to answer and none can be answered.

Controls: meta.json lists an EMPTY control array on both sides, and --probe-controls printed '(no settable controls)' for orig and port alike. Control surfaces match exactly (both empty), so there is no missing/extra/renamed/retyped dial finding.
feedback: The single actionable defect is the constant colour. Original is RGB (255,106,12); port is RGB (255,146,39). Push the port's green channel down by ~40/255 and its blue down by ~27/255 to land on the original — equivalently, drop hue from ~29.7 deg to ~23.2 deg and raise saturation from ~0.85 to ~0.95 (value stays railed at 1.0 on both). Mean brightness must come down from 147 to 124.

The colour difference reads as the port sitting at a HIGHER colour temperature / earlier point on a warm-up curve than the original. If the port maps a time-of-day (or a fixed sunrise/sunset phase) onto a colour-temperature ramp, check for an hour/offset or a units error (local vs UTC, hours vs fraction-of-day) rather than tweaking the RGB literal blind — the whole ramp may be shifted, and only one point of it is observable here.

Do NOT chase animation: the original is genuinely a static flat wash in this harness (0 motion over 480 captured frames spanning 240 s, and unchanged after 86400 s of warm-up). A port that starts animating, adds a gradient, or adds per-pixel variation would be a regression, not an improvement.
Do NOT add controls: the original exposes none, and the port correctly exposes none. Keep the control surface empty.

The time-of-day response curve is UNVERIFIABLE from output with the current harness, because wallClock is pinned and does not advance with simulated time. If the fixer wants to validate the full curve, that needs a harness ability to set the simulated wall clock (or a way to advance it with elapsed frames) — worth filing as harness work rather than guessing.
